classification.difficultyReason: The hardest part requires translating surd-labelled sides into Pythagoras’ theorem, recognising cancellation after expansion, and using positive side lengths to justify division by √(xy) before isolating y. Earlier parts support the expansion pattern but do not supply this final algebraic connection.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the exact value of $x$ in the following diagrams.

spec.description: Right triangle with unknown horizontal base, given vertical side and given hypotenuse; right angle at lower right.
spec.mathematics: Base x cm; perpendicular side 3√2 cm; hypotenuse 3√3 cm.

spec.description: Right triangle with two given perpendicular sides and unknown hypotenuse.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular sides 3√2 cm and 3√3 cm; hypotenuse x cm.

spec.description: Right triangle; each radical on a perpendicular side covers only 2.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular sides (√2−1) cm and (√2+1) cm; hypotenuse x cm.

spec.description: Right triangle; each radical on a perpendicular side covers only x.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular sides (√x−1) cm and (√x+1) cm; hypotenuse x cm.

answer.short:
$x=1+\sqrt{3}$

Use Pythagoras’ theorem and reject the negative root.
answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=(\sqrt{x}-1)^2+(\sqrt{x}+1)^2\\x^2&=(x-2\sqrt{x}+1)+(x+2\sqrt{x}+1)\\x^2&=2x+2\\x^2-2x+1&=3\\(x-1)^2&=3\\x-1&=\pm\sqrt{3}\\x&=1\pm\sqrt{3}.\end{align*}$$
Since $x$ is a positive length, reject $1-\sqrt{3}$. Hence $x=1+\sqrt{3}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the relationship between $x$ and $y$, with $y$ as the subject of the formula.

spec.description: Right triangle with surd-labelled sides. The vertical-side radical covers xy.
spec.mathematics: Base (√x−√y) cm; vertical side 2√(xy) cm; hypotenuse (√x+√y) cm.

answer.short:
$y=\dfrac{1}{x}$

Apply Pythagoras’ theorem and expand the squared surd expressions.
answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}(\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{y})^2&=(\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{y})^2+(2\sqrt{xy})^2\\x+2\sqrt{xy}+y&=x-2\sqrt{xy}+y+4xy\\4\sqrt{xy}&=4xy\\\sqrt{xy}&=xy.\end{align*}$$
The side lengths give $xy>0$, so division by $\sqrt{xy}$ is valid.
$$\begin{align*}1&=\sqrt{xy}\\xy&=1\\y&=\frac{1}{x}.\end{align*}$$
